modern: This text may not apply to more than one in a thousand of the readers of this little book of promises, but the Lord cheers that one with words like these. Let’s pray for everyone who has been wrongly thrown out of the fellowship they love. May the Lord appear to their joy!

The text applies to truly gracious people who tremble at the word of the Lord. They were hated by their own brothers and in the end thrown out because of their faithfulness and their holiness. This must have been very bitter for them, all the more because it was done in the name of religion, supposedly to glorify God. How much is done for the devil in the name of God! Using the name of the Lord to add venom to the old serpent’s bite is one example of his cunning.

The Lord’s appearing for them is the hope of his persecuted people. He appears as the advocate and defender of his chosen ones, and when he does, it means clear rescue for those who fear God and shame for their oppressors. O Lord, make this word come true for those whom people are mocking!

notes.term: Cast you out for my name’s sake
notes.note: Shut you out of the community because of your loyalty to God. Jesus warned his followers of the same ([[John.16.2|John 16:2]]).
Treat God’s word with deep, humble reverence. “To this man will I look… that trembleth at my word” ([[Isa.66.2|Isaiah 66:2]]).
Faithfulness, loyalty.
Supposedly; by their own claim.
Cunning, craftiness. “The serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field” ([[Gen.3.1|Genesis 3:1]]).
Someone who pleads another’s case.
God’s chosen people.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.

modern: No promise is made to those who give to the poor in order to be seen by others. They have their reward at once, and they can’t expect to be paid twice.

Let’s hide our giving away; yes, hide it even from ourselves. Give so often and so much, as a matter of course, that you no more notice you’ve helped the poor than that you’ve eaten your regular meals. Give without even whispering to yourself, “How generous I am!” Don’t try to reward yourself like that. Leave it with God, who never fails to see, to record and to reward. Happy is the person who is busy in secret with kindness. They find a special joy in their unknown generosity. This is the bread that, eaten in secret, is sweeter than the banquets of kings. How can I treat myself today to this delightful luxury? Let me have a real feast of tenderness and an outpouring of the soul.

Here and hereafter, the Lord himself will personally see to the rewarding of the one who gives in secret. He’ll do it in his own way and time, and he’ll choose the very best. It will take eternity to show how much this promise means.

notes.note: Gifts to the poor.
Jesus warned against giving for show: “Verily I say unto you, They have their reward” ([[Matt.6.2|Matthew 6:2]]).
Acts of kindness and generosity.
Eaten in secret. Spurgeon turns around [[Prov.9.17|Proverbs 9:17]], “bread eaten in secret is pleasant,” said there of forbidden pleasure.
Warm, open-hearted fellowship, from a well-known line of Alexander Pope.

modern: This word is truly fulfilled in the Lord Jesus, but it also applies, with a difference, to everyone who is in him. Our soul won’t be left in the state of the dead apart from the body, and our body, even if it sees decay, will rise again. But it’s the general meaning, more than this particular application, that we want our readers to think about now.

We may sink very low in spirit, until we seem to be plunged into the pit of hell, but we won’t be left there. We may seem to be at death’s door in heart and soul and mind, but we can’t stay there. Our inner death, as far as joy and hope go, may go very far, but it can’t run on to its full end and reach the complete decay of black despair. We may go very low, but no lower than the Lord allows. We may stay in the deepest dungeon of doubt for a while, but we won’t perish there. The star of hope is still in the sky when the night is blackest. The Lord won’t forget us and hand us over to the enemy. Let’s rest in hope. We’re dealing with One whose mercy lasts forever. Surely, out of death and darkness and despair, we’ll rise again to life and light and freedom.

notes.note: Here the King James uses it for the grave, the world of the dead (Hebrew *sheol*). Peter applied this verse to the resurrection of Jesus ([[Acts.2.27|Acts 2:27]]).
Allow.
Decay of the body after death.
The condition of the soul after death, separated from the body until the resurrection.
The refrain of [[Ps.136.1|Psalm 136]].

modern: Do I make the honor of God the great aim of my life and the rule of my conduct? If so, he will honor me. For a while I may get no honor from people, but God himself will honor me in the most effective way. In the end, being willing to be put to shame for conscience’ sake will turn out to be the surest way to honor.

Eli hadn’t honored the Lord by ruling his household well, and his sons hadn’t honored the Lord by behaving in a way worthy of their sacred office. So the Lord didn’t honor them. He took the high priesthood away from their family, and made young Samuel ruler in the land instead of any of their line. If I want my family to be honored, I must honor the Lord in everything. God may let the wicked win worldly honors, but the dignity he himself gives, glory and honor and immortality, he keeps for those who, by holy obedience, take care to honor him.

What can I do today to honor the Lord? I’ll promote his glory by what I say and by what I do in obedience. I’ll also honor him with my money and possessions, and by offering him some special service. Let me sit down and think how I can honor him, since he will honor me.

notes.term: “Them that honor me I will honor”
notes.note: God’s message to the priest Eli, whose sons were corrupt ([[1Sam.2.29-1Sam.2.30|1 Samuel 2:29–30]]).
Effective; actually doing what it sets out to do.
Because your conscience requires it.
The boy who served in the temple under Eli and grew up to lead Israel ([[1Sam.3.19-1Sam.3.20|1 Samuel 3:19–20]]).
Honored, raised in dignity.
From [[Rom.2.7|Romans 2:7]].
Money and possessions. “Honour the LORD with thy substance” ([[Prov.3.9|Proverbs 3:9]]).

modern: The just person fears the Lord, and so comes under God’s protection, even down to the roof over their family. Their home is a place of love, a school of holy training and a place of heavenly light. In it there’s a family altar where the name of the Lord is honored every day. So the Lord blesses their home. It may be a humble cottage or a grand mansion, but the Lord’s blessing comes because of the character of the people who live there, not because of the size of the house.

The most blessed house is the one where the master and mistress fear God. But a son or daughter, or even a servant, can bring a blessing on a whole household. The Lord often protects, prospers and provides for a family for the sake of one or two in it whom he counts just, because his grace has made them so. Dear friends, let’s have Jesus as our constant guest, as the sisters of Bethany did, and then we’ll be blessed indeed.
Let’s make sure we’re just in everything: in our business, in our judgment of others, in how we treat our neighbors and in our own personal character. A just God can’t bless unjust dealings.

notes.note: A home, a dwelling place.
Those who are right with God and live rightly.
Home.
Daily family worship: reading the Bible and praying together at home.

notes.term: For the sake of one or two in it
notes.note: As God blessed Potiphar’s house “for Joseph’s sake” ([[Gen.39.5|Genesis 39:5]]).
Martha and Mary, who often welcomed Jesus into their home ([[Luke.10.38-Luke.10.39|Luke 10:38–39]]).

modern: This is an excellent reason for throwing away every other confidence and relying on the Lord alone. When a child is left without its natural protector, our God steps in and becomes its guardian. In the same way, when someone has lost everything they used to depend on, they can throw themselves on the living God and find in him everything they need. Orphans are thrown on God’s fatherhood, and he provides for them. The writer of these pages knows what it is to hang on the bare arm of God, and he gladly bears witness that no trust is so well backed up by the facts, or so sure to be rewarded by the results, as trust in the invisible but ever-living God.

Some children who have fathers aren’t much better off for it, but the fatherless who have God are rich. Better to have God and no other friend than all the patrons on earth and no God. Losing a human support is painful, but as long as the Lord stays the fountain of mercy for us, we aren’t really orphaned. Let fatherless children plead this gracious word today, and let everyone who has lost their visible support do the same. Lord, let me find mercy in you! The more needy and helpless I am, the more confidently I appeal to your loving heart.

notes.note: Orphans. God calls himself “a father of the fatherless” ([[Ps.68.5|Psalm 68:5]]).
Spurgeon himself.
God’s power alone, with nothing else to lean on. “The LORD hath made bare his holy arm” ([[Isa.52.10|Isaiah 52:10]]).
Justified, backed up.
Wealthy, powerful supporters.
Losing a human being, or anything God has made, that we leaned on.

modern: He has done it. Remember Joseph, Israel in Egypt, Manasseh, Jeremiah, Peter and many others. He can still do it. He breaks the bars of brass with a word and snaps the chains of iron with a look. He is doing it. In a thousand places troubled people are coming out into light and freedom. Jesus still announces the opening of the prison to those who are bound. At this very moment doors are swinging open and chains are dropping to the ground.

He will love to set you free, dear friend, if right now you’re grieving because of sorrow, doubt and fear. It will be a joy to Jesus to give you freedom. It will give him as much pleasure to set you loose as it will give you to be set loose. No, you don’t have to snap the iron band. The Lord himself will do it. Only trust him, and he will be your Liberator. Believe in him in spite of the stone walls and the iron handcuffs. Satan can’t hold you, sin can’t chain you, even despair can’t bind you, if you’ll believe right now in the Lord Jesus, in how free his grace is and how complete his power to save.
Defy the enemy, and let the word in front of you now be your song of deliverance: “Jehovah looseth the prisoners.”

notes.note: Sets free.

All freed from prison by God: Joseph in Egypt ([[Gen.41.14|Genesis 41:14]]), King Manasseh from Babylon after he repented ([[2Chr.33.12-2Chr.33.13|2 Chronicles 33:12–13]]), Jeremiah from the dungeon ([[Jer.38.13|Jeremiah 38:13]]) and Peter by an angel ([[Acts.12.7|Acts 12:7]]).

notes.term: Bars of brass… fetters of iron
notes.note: “He hath broken the gates of brass, and cut the bars of iron in sunder” ([[Ps.107.16|Psalm 107:16]]).
Freedom, room to move.
From [[Isa.61.1|Isaiah 61:1]], which Jesus read out as his own mission ([[Luke.4.18|Luke 4:18]]).
Liberator; one who sets slaves free.
Handcuffs.

modern: Obedience brings a blessing on all the provisions our hard work earns us. What comes in and goes straight out again, like fruit in a basket meant for eating right away, will be blessed, and what we put by for a longer time will be blessed just the same. Perhaps ours is a handbasket share. We have a little for breakfast, and a meager bite for lunch in a basket when we go out to work in the morning. That’s fine, because God’s blessing is promised to the basket. If we live from hand to mouth, getting each day’s supply on the day, we’re as well off as Israel was, because when the Lord fed his favored people, he only gave them one day’s manna at a time. What more did they need? What more do we need?

But if we do have savings, how much we need the Lord to bless them! There’s the worry of getting, the worry of keeping, the worry of managing and the worry of using. And unless the Lord blesses it, these worries will eat into our hearts until our goods become our gods and our cares become cankers.
O Lord, bless our possessions. Help us to use them for your glory. Help us to keep worldly things in their proper places, and may our savings never endanger the saving of our souls.

notes.note: Savings; what is stored up.
Hard work.
With just enough for today and nothing put by.

notes.term: A day’s manna at a time
notes.note: Israel was told to gather only one day’s manna, and what was kept overnight went bad ([[Exod.16.19-Exod.16.20|Exodus 16:19–20]]).
Spreading sores or rot that eat away at something.
Money and possessions.

modern: The principle in this text suggests that all of us who are the Lord’s strangers and foreigners should want to promote the peace and prosperity of the people we live among. Above all, our nation and our city should be blessed by our constant prayers for them. An earnest prayer for your own country and for other countries is very fitting for every believer.

Let’s pray eagerly for the great gift of peace, both at home and abroad. If conflict caused bloodshed in our streets, or if war abroad killed our brave soldiers, we would all grieve over the disaster. So let’s pray for peace, and work hard to promote the principles that can bind together the classes at home and the races abroad in friendship.

We’re promised quiet ourselves along with the peace of the nation, and that’s most desirable, because then we can bring up our families in the fear of the Lord and preach the gospel freely. Today let’s pray much for our country, confessing the nation’s sins and asking for the nation’s pardon and blessing, for Jesus’ sake.

notes.note: Jeremiah wrote to the Jews taken into exile in Babylon, telling them to settle down and pray for the city they now lived in ([[Jer.29.4-Jer.29.7|Jeremiah 29:4–7]]).
Believers are “strangers and pilgrims on the earth,” whose true home is heaven ([[Heb.11.13|Hebrews 11:13]]).
Praying for someone else.
A gift, a blessing.
Friendship, good relations.
Freely, with nothing to stop us. “Let” is an old word for an obstacle.

modern: This world is as dark as midnight. Jesus has come so that by faith we can have light, and no longer sit in the gloom that covers the rest of humanity.

“Whosoever” is a very wide word. It means you and me. If we trust in Jesus, we’ll no longer sit in the dark shadow of death, but come out into the warm light of a day that will never end. Why don’t we come out into the light right away?

A cloud may sometimes hang over us, but we won’t stay in darkness if we believe in Jesus. He has come to give us broad daylight. Will he come in vain? If we have faith, we have the privilege of sunlight; let’s enjoy it. Jesus has come to set us free from the night of our fallen nature, of ignorance, of doubt, of despair, of sin and of dread. And all believers will find that he no more comes in vain than the sun rises without spreading its heat and light.

Shake off your gloom, dear friend. Don’t stay in the dark; stay in the light. Your hope, your joy and your heaven are in Jesus. Look to him, and only to him, and you’ll rejoice as the birds rejoice at sunrise, and as the angels rejoice before the throne.

notes.note: Stay, remain.
Whoever; anyone at all.
“The people which sat in darkness saw great light; and to them which sat in the region and shadow of death light is sprung up” ([[Matt.4.16|Matthew 4:16]]).
The sinfulness of our nature as we’re born.

modern: Let this be settled: the battle is the Lord’s, and we can be quite sure of victory, and of victory in a way that will best of all show the power of God. Everyone forgets the Lord far too much, yes, even the gatherings of Israel. And when there’s a chance to make people see that the Great First Cause can achieve his purposes without human power, it’s a priceless opportunity that should be well used. Even Israel looks too much to sword and spear. It’s a grand thing for David to have no sword in his hand, and yet to know that his God will overthrow a whole army of foreigners.

If we really are fighting for truth and righteousness, let’s not wait until we have talent or wealth or any other visible power at our disposal. With whatever stones we find in the brook, and with our own ordinary sling, let’s run to meet the enemy. If it were our own battle, we might not be confident. But if we’re standing up for Jesus and fighting in his strength alone, who can stand against us? Without a trace of hesitation, let’s face the Philistines, because the Lord of hosts is with us, and who can be against us?

notes.note: David’s words to Goliath before he killed him with a sling and a stone ([[1Sam.17.47|1 Samuel 17:47]]).
God, the cause of all things, who needs nothing else to act.
Foreigners.
Wait, delay.
David chose “five smooth stones out of the brook” ([[1Sam.17.40|1 Samuel 17:40]]).
God as commander of the armies of heaven.
“If God be for us, who can be against us?” ([[Rom.8.31|Romans 8:31]]).

modern: The blessings of the tribes are ours, because we’re the true Israel who worship God in the spirit and put no confidence in the flesh. Zebulun is to rejoice because the Lord will bless his “going out,” and we can see a promise for ourselves hidden in this blessing too. When we go out, we’ll look out for reasons to be glad.

We go out to travel, and God’s providence is our escort. We go out to emigrate, and the Lord is with us on land and sea. We go out as missionaries, and Jesus says, “Lo, I am with you unto the end of the world.” We go out every day to our work, and we can do it with pleasure, because God will be with us from morning till evening.

Sometimes a fear creeps over us as we set out, because we don’t know what we may meet. But this blessing can serve us very well as a word of good cheer. As we pack up to move, let’s put this verse in our traveling trunk. Let’s drop it into our hearts and keep it there. Yes, let’s lay it on our tongues to make us sing. Let’s weigh anchor with a song, or jump into the carriage with a psalm. Let’s belong to the rejoicing tribe, and praise the Lord with joyful hearts in every move we make.

notes.note: One of the twelve tribes of Israel, a seafaring tribe. This is Moses’ blessing on it before he died ([[Deut.33.18-Deut.33.19|Deuteronomy 33:18–19]]).
“We are the circumcision, which worship God in the spirit, and rejoice in Christ Jesus, and have no confidence in the flesh” ([[Phil.3.3|Philippians 3:3]]).
Hidden, present but not yet seen.
A blessing.
An escort for protection on a journey.
Pull up the anchor and set sail.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.

modern: Jeremiah was young, and he naturally shrank back when the Lord sent him on a great errand. But the One who sent him wouldn’t let him say, “I am a child.” What he was in himself wasn’t to be mentioned. It was to be lost in the thought that he had been chosen to speak for God. He didn’t have to think up and invent a message, or choose an audience. He was to speak what God commanded, and speak where God sent him, and he would be able to do this in a strength not his own.

Isn’t it the same with some young preacher or teacher reading these lines? God knows how young you are, and how thin your knowledge and experience are. But if he chooses to send you, it isn’t for you to shrink from the heavenly call. God will show his greatness in your weakness. If you were as old as Methuselah, how much would your years help you? If you were as wise as Solomon, you might be just as headstrong as he was. Stick to your message, and that will be your wisdom. Follow your marching orders, and they will be your good judgment.

notes.note: Jeremiah’s protest when God called him to be a prophet ([[Jer.1.6-Jer.1.7|Jeremiah 1:6–7]]).
The longest-lived man in the Bible, who lived 969 years ([[Gen.5.27|Genesis 5:27]]).
Solomon, for all his wisdom, let his many wives turn his heart to other gods in his old age ([[1Kgs.11.4|1 Kings 11:4]]).
Good judgment; wisdom in what to do.

modern: A mother’s comfort! Ah, this is tenderness itself. How she enters into her child’s grief! How she holds him to her chest and tries to take all his sorrow into her own heart! He can tell her everything, and she’ll understand as nobody else can. Of all comforters, a child loves his mother best, and even grown men have found it so.

Does the Lord stoop to play the mother’s part? This is goodness indeed. We easily see how he is a father, but will he be like a mother too? Doesn’t this invite us to holy closeness, to complete trust, to sacred rest? When God himself becomes “the Comforter,” no anguish can last long. Let’s pour out our trouble, even if sobs and sighs are the easiest way we can say it. He won’t despise us for our tears; our mother didn’t. He’ll make allowance for our weakness as she did, and he’ll put away our faults, only in a surer, safer way than our mother could. We won’t try to bear our grief alone. That would be unkind to someone so gentle and kind. Let’s begin the day with our loving God, and why shouldn’t we end it in the same company, since mothers never tire of their children?

notes.note: The chest, the place of closest embrace.
Stoop down kindly from a high position.
The Holy Spirit; Jesus’ name for him in [[John.14.26|John 14:26]].
Last, remain.

notes.term: Mothers weary not of their children
notes.note: “Can a woman forget her sucking child?… yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee” ([[Isa.49.15|Isaiah 49:15]]).

modern: Shut out from the public means of grace, we aren’t shut out from the grace those means bring. The Lord who puts his people where they feel like exiles will be with them himself, and be everything to them they could have had at home in their holy gatherings. Take this to heart, you who are called to wander!

God is a place of refuge for his people. They find sanctuary in him from every enemy. He is their place of worship too. He is with them as he was with Jacob when he slept in the open field, and got up and said, “Surely God was in this place.” To them he will also be a sanctuary of quiet, like the Most Holy Place, the silent dwelling of the Eternal. They’ll be at peace, free from fear of evil.

God himself, in Christ Jesus, is the sanctuary of mercy. The Lord Jesus is the ark of the covenant, and Aaron’s rod, the pot of manna and the tablets of the law are all in Christ our sanctuary. In God we find the shrine of holiness and of fellowship. What more do we need? O Lord, keep this promise and always be to us like a little sanctuary!

notes.note: God’s promise to the exiles in Babylon, far from the temple in Jerusalem ([[Ezek.11.16|Ezekiel 11:16]]).
The ordinary ways God feeds faith: the Bible, prayer, preaching, the Lord’s Supper.
Holy gatherings for worship.
Jacob’s words after his dream at Bethel, where he had slept in the open with a stone for a pillow. The King James reads “Surely the LORD is in this place” ([[Gen.28.16|Genesis 28:16]]).
The innermost room of the tabernacle and temple, where God’s presence was.
Dwelling place.

notes.term: Aaron’s rod, the pot of manna, the tables of the law
notes.note: The things kept in or beside the ark of the covenant ([[Heb.9.4|Hebrews 9:4]]).
Close fellowship and sharing, with God or with each other.

modern: It’s a good thing when someone can be copied in such detail with as much benefit as Paul could. Oh, for grace to imitate him today and every day!

If, by God’s grace, we put Paul’s teaching into practice, we can claim the promise in front of us now, and what a promise it is! God, who loves peace, makes peace and breathes peace, will be with us. “Peace be with you” is a sweet blessing, but for the God of peace to be with us is far more. Then we have the fountain as well as the streams, the sun as well as its beams. If the God of peace is with us, we’ll enjoy the peace of God that passes all understanding, even when outward circumstances threaten to disturb us. If people quarrel, we’ll be sure to be peacemakers, if the Maker of peace is with us.

Real peace is found on the road of truth. If we give up the faith or leave the path of righteousness with the idea of promoting peace, we’ll be badly mistaken. First pure, then peaceable: that’s the order of wisdom and of fact. Let’s keep to Paul’s line, and we’ll have the God of peace with us, as he was with the apostle.

notes.note: An old word for an example.
In the smallest details.
Of Paul; Paul’s.
A blessing.

notes.term: The peace of God which passeth all understanding
notes.note: [[Phil.4.7|Philippians 4:7]], just before the day’s text.
“The wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable” ([[Jas.3.17|James 3:17]]).

modern: Whenever fear comes in and makes us falter, we’re in danger of falling into sin. Conceit is to be dreaded, but so is cowardice. “Dare to be a Daniel.” Our great Captain should be served by brave soldiers.

What a reason for bravery this is! God is with those who are with him. God will never be missing when the hour of struggle comes. Are they threatening you? Who are you to be afraid of a man who will die? Will you lose your job? The God you serve will find bread and water for his servants. Can’t you trust him? Are they pouring ridicule on you? Will that break your bones, or your heart? Bear it for Christ’s sake, and even rejoice because of it.

God is with the true, the just and the holy to rescue them, and he’ll rescue you. Remember how Daniel came out of the lions’ den, and the three holy young men out of the furnace. Your case isn’t as desperate as theirs, but if it were, the Lord would carry you through and make you more than a conqueror. Fear to fear. Be afraid of being afraid. Your worst enemy is inside your own chest. Get on your knees and cry for help, and then get up saying, “I will trust, and not be afraid.”

notes.term: Be not afraid of their faces
notes.note: God’s words to the young Jeremiah as he sent him to speak ([[Jer.1.8|Jeremiah 1:8]]).
From a popular hymn of Spurgeon’s day by Philip Bliss, “Dare to be a Daniel, dare to stand alone.”
“Who art thou, that thou shouldest be afraid of a man that shall die?” ([[Isa.51.12|Isaiah 51:12]]).
Job, position.
Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, who came out of Nebuchadnezzar’s fiery furnace unharmed ([[Dan.3.26-Dan.3.27|Daniel 3:26–27]]).
“In all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us” ([[Rom.8.37|Romans 8:37]]).
The chest; the heart.

notes.term: “I will trust, and not be afraid”

modern: This is as good as a promise, because it states a present fact that will stay the same for all time. God takes great pleasure in the prayers of upright people. He even calls them his delight. Our first concern is to be upright. Don’t bend this way or that; keep upright. Not crooked with scheming, not flat on your face by giving in to evil, but upright in strict honesty and straightforwardness. If we start to dodge and wriggle, we’ll be left to fend for ourselves. If we try crooked ways, we’ll find we can’t pray, and if we pretend to, we’ll find our prayers shut out of heaven.

Are we going in a straight line, following the Lord’s revealed will? Then let’s pray much and pray in faith. If our prayer is God’s delight, let’s not be stingy with what gives him pleasure. He doesn’t look at its grammar, or its philosophy, or its eloquence; in all those things people might despise it. Like a father, he takes pleasure in the babbling of his own babies, the stammering of his newborn sons and daughters. Shouldn’t we delight in prayer, since the Lord delights in it? Let’s find errands to take to the throne. The Lord gives us plenty of reasons to pray, and we ought to thank him that he does.

notes.note: Scheming, cunning.
Lying face down.
Dodge and evade; act deceitfully.
Fend for ourselves, manage alone.
Give too little; hold back.
Philosophy; deep reasoning.
A small child’s first, unclear words.

modern: Grace is what we need right now, and it can be had freely. What could be freer than a gift? Today we’ll receive grace that holds us up, strengthens us, makes us holy and satisfies us. He has given grace every day until now, and as for the future, that grace is still enough. If we have only a little grace, the fault must lie with us, because the Lord isn’t limited, and he isn’t slow to give it in abundance. We can ask for as much as we want and never fear a refusal. He gives generously and doesn’t scold.

The Lord may not give gold, but he will give grace. He may not give profit, but he will give grace. He will certainly send us trials, but he’ll give grace to match them. We may be called to work and to suffer, but with the call will come all the grace we need.

What an AND there is in the text: “and glory!” We don’t need glory yet, and we aren’t fit for it yet, but we’ll have it in due order. After we’ve eaten the bread of grace, we’ll drink the wine of glory. We must go through the Holy Place, which is grace, to the Most Holy Place, which is glory. These words, “and glory,” are enough to make a person dance for joy. A little while, a little while, and then glory forever!

notes.note: Making holy.
Limited, held back.

notes.term: He giveth liberally and upbraideth not
notes.note: He gives generously and doesn’t scold ([[Jas.1.5|James 1:5]]).

notes.term: The holy… the holiest of all
notes.note: The two rooms of the tabernacle: the Holy Place, and the Most Holy Place behind the veil, where God’s presence was ([[Heb.9.2-Heb.9.3|Hebrews 9:2–3]]).

modern: Clothes are expensive, and poor believers may get anxious about where their next suit will come from. The soles are thin; how will we get new shoes? See how our thoughtful Lord has provided against this worry. Our heavenly Father clothes the grass of the field with a splendor Solomon couldn’t match. Won’t he clothe his own children? We’re sure he will. There may be many a patch and darn, but we’ll have clothes.

A poor minister found his clothes nearly threadbare, so worn they would hardly hold together. But as a servant of the Lord, he expected his Master to provide his uniform. It so happened that the writer, visiting a friend, was lent this good man’s pulpit, and it came into his mind to take up a collection for him, and there was his suit. We’ve seen many other cases where those who served the Lord found him thoughtful about their wardrobe. The One who made man so that, once he had sinned, he needed clothes, also mercifully supplied them. And the clothes the Lord gave our first parents were far better than the ones they made for themselves.

notes.note: Dried grass was used as fuel for clay ovens.
Jesus’ gentle rebuke to his anxious disciples ([[Matt.6.30|Matthew 6:30]]).
“Even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these” ([[Matt.6.29|Matthew 6:29]]).
Clothing.
The uniform worn by the servants of a great household.
Spurgeon himself.

notes.term: Those which the Lord gave our first parents
notes.note: Adam and Eve sewed fig leaves together, but God made them coats of skins ([[Gen.3.7|Genesis 3:7]]; [[Gen.3.21|Genesis 3:21]]).

modern: That is, if we follow the ways of wisdom and holiness, we’ll be kept safe in them. Someone traveling the highway in daylight has some protection. Every person has a road, their own proper calling in life, and if we walk it faithfully in the fear of God, he will keep *us* from evil. We may not travel in luxury, but we’ll walk safely. We may not be able to run like young men, but we’ll be able to walk like good men.

Our greatest danger lies in ourselves. Our weak feet are so sadly quick to stumble. Let’s ask for more moral strength, so that our tendency to slip can be overcome. Some stumble because they don’t see the stone in the road. God’s grace lets us see sin, and so avoid it. Let’s plead this promise and trust in the One who holds up his chosen.
Sadly, our worst danger is our own carelessness, but the Lord Jesus has put us on guard against this, saying, “Watch and pray.”

Oh, for grace to walk today without a single stumble! It isn’t enough that we don’t actually fall. Our cry should be that our feet won’t make the smallest slip, and that at the end we may worship the One “who is able to keep us from stumbling.”

notes.term: Then shalt thou walk in thy way safely
notes.note: The reward of keeping wisdom and good sense ([[Prov.3.21-Prov.3.23|Proverbs 3:21–23]]).
Your own particular work and place in life.
“Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation” ([[Matt.26.41|Matthew 26:41]]).

notes.term: “Who is able to keep us from stumbling”
notes.note: From [[Jude.1.24|Jude 24]], where the King James reads “able to keep you from falling.”

modern: Humble hearts look for grace, and so they get it. Humble hearts give way to the sweet influences of grace, and so it’s given to them more and more freely. Humble hearts lie in the valleys where the streams of grace are flowing, and so they drink from them. Humble hearts are grateful for grace and give the Lord the glory for it, and so it fits his honor to give it to them.

Come, dear reader, take a lowly place. Be little in your own eyes, so that the Lord may make much of you. Perhaps a sigh breaks out: “I fear I am not humble.” It may be that this is the language of true humility. Some are proud of being humble, and this is one of the very worst kinds of pride. We are needy, helpless, undeserving, hell-deserving creatures, and if we aren’t humble, we ought to be. Let’s humble ourselves because of our sins against humility, and then the Lord will let us taste his favor. It’s grace that makes us humble, and grace that finds in this humility a chance to pour in more grace. Let’s go down so that we may rise. Let’s be poor in spirit so that God may make us rich. Let’s be humble so that we won’t need to be humbled, but may be lifted up by the grace of God.

notes.term: He giveth grace unto the humble
notes.note: “God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble” ([[Jas.4.6|James 4:6]]; also [[1Pet.5.5|1 Peter 5:5]]).
Opinion; how highly you rate something.
“Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven” ([[Matt.5.3|Matthew 5:3]]).
Lifted up. “He that humbleth himself shall be exalted” ([[Luke.14.11|Luke 14:11]]).

modern: Think of the infinitely glorious Jehovah acting as a guide to the blind! What boundless condescension this means! A blind man can’t find a way he doesn’t know. Even when he knows the road, it’s hard for him to travel it; but a road he has never known is out of the question for his unguided feet. Now, by nature we are blind about the way of salvation, and yet the Lord leads us into it, and brings us to himself, and then opens our eyes. As for the future, we’re all blind and can’t see an hour ahead; but the Lord Jesus will lead us all the way to our journey’s end. Blessed be his name!

We can’t guess how deliverance could possibly come to us, but the Lord knows, and he will lead us until we’ve escaped every danger. Happy are those who put their hand in the hand of the great Guide, and leave their way and themselves entirely with him. He’ll bring them all the way. And when he has brought them home to glory and opened their eyes to see the way he led them, what a song of gratitude they’ll sing to their great Benefactor! Lord, lead your poor blind child today, for I don’t know my way!

notes.term: I will bring the blind by a way that they knew not
notes.note: The verse goes on, “I will make darkness light before them, and crooked things straight” ([[Isa.42.16|Isaiah 42:16]]).
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
Stooping down from a high position, in the good sense, without today’s sense of looking down on someone.
Travel across.
One who does good to another; a generous giver.

modern: People are often as lacking in reason as in faith. We still have “unreasonable and wicked men” among us. There’s no use arguing with them or trying to be at peace with them. They are false at heart and deceitful in speech. Well, what of it? Shall we worry ourselves over them? No; let’s turn to the Lord, for he is faithful. No promise from his Word will ever be broken. He is neither unreasonable in his demands on us nor unfaithful to our claims on him. We have a faithful God. Let that be our joy.

He will establish us so that wicked people won’t bring us down, and he will keep us so that none of the evils now attacking us will really do us harm. What a blessing for us that we don’t need to fight with people, but are allowed to shelter in the Lord Jesus, who feels with us more truly than anyone. There is one true heart, one faithful mind, one never-changing Love; let’s rest there. The Lord will carry out the purpose of his grace toward us, his servants, and we needn’t let a shadow of fear fall on our spirits. Nothing that people or devils can do can keep us from God’s protection and provision. Today let’s pray for the Lord to establish us and keep us.

notes.note: Paul asks prayer “that we may be delivered from unreasonable and wicked men: for all men have not faith” ([[2Thess.3.2|2 Thessalonians 3:2]]). The promise follows in the next verse.
Establish; make firm and steady.
Keep us from.

modern: Are you, dear reader, likely to be kept in bed for a while by sickness? Then go upstairs without distress, with this promise on your heart: “When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid.”

When we go to bed at night, let this word smooth our pillow. We can’t guard ourselves while we sleep, but the Lord will keep us through the night. Those who lie down under the Lord’s protection are as safe as kings and queens in their palaces, and a great deal safer. If, as we lie down, we also lay down all our worries and ambitions, we’ll get a refreshing from our beds such as the anxious and greedy never find in theirs. Bad dreams will be banished; or even if they come, we’ll shake off the impression they leave, knowing that they’re only dreams.

If we sleep like this, we’ll do well. How sweetly Peter slept when even the angel’s light didn’t wake him, and he needed a hard nudge in the side to wake up. And yet he was sentenced to die the next day. In the same way, martyrs have slept before they were burned. “So he giveth his beloved sleep.”
To have sweet sleep we must have sweet lives, sweet tempers, sweet meditations and sweet love.

notes.note: Lie. “When thou liest down” means “when you lie down.”
Greedy for more than you have.
Herod meant to kill Peter, but the night before, Peter slept between two soldiers until an angel struck him on the side to wake him ([[Acts.12.6-Acts.12.7|Acts 12:6–7]]).
The next day.

modern: Remember that this is a promise to the person who considers the poor. Are you one of them? Then take the text home.

See how, in the hour of sickness, the God of the poor will bless the one who cares for the poor! The everlasting arms will hold up his soul, the way friendly hands and soft pillows hold up the body of the sick. How tender and sympathetic this picture is; how near it brings our God to our weaknesses and sicknesses! Whoever heard this said of the old pagan god Jove, or of the gods of India or China? This is language belonging only to the God of Israel. He is the one who stoops to become nurse and attendant to good people. If he strikes with one hand, he holds up with the other. Oh, it’s a blessed fainting when you fall on the Lord’s own bosom and are carried there! Grace is the best of medicines. Divine love is the safest tonic for a weak and failing patient: it makes the soul as strong as a giant, even when the bones are almost breaking through the skin. There’s no doctor like the Lord, no tonic like his promise, no wine like his love.
Dear reader, if you have failed in your duty to the poor, see what you’re losing, and become their friend and helper at once.

notes.term: The man who considers the poor
notes.note: The psalm begins, “Blessed is he that considereth the poor: the LORD will deliver him in time of trouble” ([[Ps.41.1|Psalm 41:1]]).
A sickbed, where someone lies weak and wasting.
“The eternal God is thy refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms” ([[Deut.33.27|Deuteronomy 33:27]]).
Jupiter, the chief god of the Romans.
Graciously chooses, stoops to.
The chest, the place of closest embrace.
Medicines that bring back strength.

modern: The nearer we come to God, the more graciously he will show himself to us. When the prodigal comes to his father, his father runs to meet him. When the wandering dove returns to the ark, Noah puts out his hand and pulls her in to him. When the loving wife seeks her husband’s company, he comes to her on wings of love. Come then, dear friend, let’s draw near to God, who waits for us so graciously, and even comes to meet us.

Have you ever noticed that passage in [[Isa.58.9|Isaiah 58:9]]? There the Lord seems to put himself at his people’s disposal, saying to them, “Here I am.” As if to say, “What do you have to say to me? What can I do for you? I’m waiting to bless you.” How can we hesitate to draw near? God is near to forgive, to bless, to comfort, to help, to make alive, to deliver. Let it be our main concern to get near to God. Once this is done, everything is done. If we draw near to others, they may soon grow tired of us and leave us. But if we seek the Lord alone, no change will come over his mind, and he’ll keep coming nearer and nearer to us in fuller and more joyful fellowship.

notes.note: Come near.
The wasteful son in Jesus’ parable. “When he was yet a great way off, his father saw him… and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him” ([[Luke.15.20|Luke 15:20]]).
The dove Noah sent from the ark found no rest, “then he put forth his hand, and took her, and pulled her in unto him into the ark” ([[Gen.8.9|Genesis 8:9]]).
Company.
“Then shalt thou call, and the LORD shall answer; thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am” ([[Isa.58.9|Isaiah 58:9]]).
To make alive. “Quick” once meant “living”, as in “the quick and the dead”.

modern: If we obey the Lord, he will make our enemies see that his blessing rests on us. Though this is a promise of the law, it still holds good for the people of God, for Jesus has removed the curse, but he has made the blessing secure.

It’s for saints to lead the way among people by holy influence. They are not to be the tail, dragged this way and that by others. We mustn’t give way to the spirit of the age, but make the age bow to Christ. If the Lord is with us, we won’t beg for religion to be tolerated; we’ll seek to seat it on the throne of society. Hasn’t the Lord Jesus made his people priests? Surely they are to teach, and mustn’t take lessons from the philosophies of unbelievers. Aren’t we made kings in Christ, to reign on the earth? How, then, can we be the servants of custom, the slaves of human opinion?

Dear friend, have you taken up your true position for Jesus? Too many keep quiet because they’re shy, if not cowardly. Should we let the name of the Lord Jesus be kept in the background? Should our religion trail along like a tail? Shouldn’t it rather lead the way, and be the ruling force in ourselves and others?

notes.note: One of the blessings Moses promised Israel “if thou hearken unto the commandments of the LORD thy God” ([[Deut.28.13|Deuteronomy 28:13]]).
“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us” ([[Gal.3.13|Galatians 3:13]]).
Here and there; this way and that.
Being put up with, allowed to exist.
Christ “hath made us unto our God kings and priests: and we shall reign on the earth” ([[Rev.5.10|Revelation 5:10]]).
Shy; lacking confidence.

modern: As long as the Lord had work for Paul to do in Corinth, the fury of the mob was held back. The Jews opposed him and blasphemed, but they could stop neither the preaching of the gospel nor the conversion of those who heard it. God has power over the most violent minds. He makes the wrath of man praise him when it breaks out, but he shows his goodness even more when he holds it back; and he can hold it back. “By the greatness of thine arm they shall be as still as a stone, till thy people pass over, O Lord.”

So don’t be afraid of anyone when you know you’re doing your duty. Go straight on, as Jesus would have done, and those who oppose you will be like a bruised reed and smoking flax. Many a time people have had cause to fear because they were afraid themselves; but a fearless faith in God brushes fear aside like the cobwebs in a giant’s path. No one can harm us unless the Lord allows it. He who makes the devil himself run away at a word can certainly control the devil’s agents. Maybe they’re already more afraid of you than you are of them. So go forward, and where you expected to meet enemies you will find friends.

notes.note: The Lord’s words to Paul in a vision at night in Corinth, where he had been opposed ([[Acts.18.9-Acts.18.10|Acts 18:9–10]]).
Attack you.

notes.term: The wrath of man to praise Him
notes.note: “Surely the wrath of man shall praise thee: the remainder of wrath shalt thou restrain” ([[Ps.76.10|Psalm 76:10]]).
From Moses’ song after the Red Sea crossing ([[Exod.15.16|Exodus 15:16]]).
Pictures of weakness, from [[Isa.42.3|Isaiah 42:3]].
Fearless.

notes.term: Makes the devil himself to flee
notes.note: “Resist the devil, and he will flee from you” ([[Jas.4.7|James 4:7]]).

modern: No worry, but all prayer. No anxiety, but plenty of joyful fellowship with God. Take your desires to the Lord of your life, the guardian of your soul. Go to him with two portions of prayer and one of fragrant praise. Don’t pray doubtfully, but thankfully. Consider that you already have what you asked for, and so thank God for his grace. He is giving you grace; give him thanks. Hide nothing. Let no need lie festering in your heart; “make known your requests.” Don’t run to people. Go only to your God, the Father of Jesus, who loves you in him.

This will bring you God’s own peace. You won’t be able to understand the peace you’ll enjoy. It will wrap you in its infinite embrace. Your heart and mind, through Christ Jesus, will be soaked in a sea of rest. Come life or death, poverty, pain or slander, you will live in Jesus, above every ruffling wind and darkening cloud. Won’t you obey this dear command?
Yes, Lord, I do believe you; but I beg you, help my unbelief.

notes.note: Don’t be anxious about anything. “Careful” once meant full of care, worried.
A humble, earnest request; a prayer.
Goes beyond anything we can understand ([[Phil.4.7|Philippians 4:7]]).
Festering; going on hurting.
Spurgeon’s short form of “let your requests be made known unto God” ([[Phil.4.6|Philippians 4:6]]).
The father’s cry to Jesus: “Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief” ([[Mark.9.24|Mark 9:24]]).

modern: When God is out in the world in judgments, he doesn’t want his people to be alarmed. He hasn’t come out to harm the righteous, but to defend them.

He wants them to show courage. We who enjoy the presence of God ought to show presence of mind. Since the Lord himself may come suddenly, we shouldn’t be surprised at anything sudden. Calm in the rush and roar of unexpected evils is a precious gift of divine love.

The Lord wants his chosen to show discernment, so that they can see that the ruin of the wicked isn’t a real disaster for the universe. Sin alone is evil; the punishment that follows it is like a preserving salt that keeps society from rotting. We should be far more shocked at the sin that deserves hell than at the hell that comes from sin.

In the same way, the Lord’s people should show great quietness of spirit. Satan and his serpent seed are full of every kind of cunning; but those who walk with God won’t be caught in their deceitful traps. Go on, believer in Jesus, and let the Lord be your confidence.

notes.note: Out and active in the world.
Staying calm and thinking clearly in a sudden emergency.
Wise judgment: telling things apart rightly (not prejudice).
Ruin.
The serpent’s offspring: those who belong to Satan ([[Gen.3.15|Genesis 3:15]]).
Cunning. “The serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field” ([[Gen.3.1|Genesis 3:1]]).

notes.term: Keep thy foot from being taken
notes.note: Keep your foot from being caught, as in a trap ([[Prov.3.26|Proverbs 3:26]]).
